Here's a weekly plan built around your classes and desk shifts, ending at 2 a.m. nightly. I'll keep it tight, and I'm assuming the 10:30 Tue/Thu class runs roughly 90 minutes.

**Every weekday**
- Daytime gap: one alum LinkedIn message (15 min, between classes or on the train)
- 11:30 p.m.-11:45 p.m.: spreadsheet update (log the alum message, any apps, follow-up dates)

**Mon / Wed (desk 3-6)**
- 6:30-7:30 p.m.: dinner + break
- 7:30-9:30 p.m.: applications (1 app Mon, 1 app Wed, tailored)
- 9:30-11:30 p.m.: tote-flow project work
- 11:30-11:45 p.m.: spreadsheet
- 11:45 p.m.-1:30 a.m.: resume tweaks or reading (flexible)
- 1:30-2 a.m.: wind down, done

**Tue / Thu (no desk shift)**
- 1:00-3:00 p.m.: applications (1 app Tue, 1 app Thu, plus research)
- 7:00-9:30 p.m.: tote-flow project (meet with group if you can)
- 9:30-11:30 p.m.: flexible, catch-up
- 11:30-11:45 p.m.: spreadsheet
- Done by 2 a.m. at the latest

**Friday (desk 1-5)**
- 6-8 p.m.: 1 app (that's your 5)
- After 8 p.m.: free

**Weekend**
- Sat: 2 hours on the project, and a 30-minute spreadsheet review/planning for next week
- Sun: light, prep for the week, nothing else scheduled

That gives you 5 apps, 5 alum messages, about 8-10 project hours, and your full desk shifts. The 2 a.m. cutoff leaves a lot of slack, so you could stop earlier on most nights if you want.
